page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz. The system includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor provides advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8). These hardware-level features accelerate matrix multiplication and vector operations. Cryptographic tasks are supported by AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, while memory and cache control are managed via CLFLUSHOPT and CLWB.

Benchmarks indicate strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2172.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.54 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4334.16 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 28.94 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, measuring 41.23 GB/sec for read-only and 29.77 GB/sec for write operations, whereas small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 321.22 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, the m8i-flex.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-speed networking. It is suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, basic database operations, and lightweight web serving. The lack of bundled local storage and modest 1 Gbps network baseline represent key tradeoffs for data-intensive or highly distributed applications.
